verdict_reason: The estimand is BLME's own, and its central correctness claim -- that the concept's LOGIT-space direction is u = W_out J_ln(h0) v, with the LayerNorm Jacobian taken at the prompt's own final hidden state -- I verified independently by ground truth. Injecting a random v at layers[-1] and measuring the ACTUAL logit change: cos(delta_logits, u) = +0.999919 (gpt2), +0.989663 (pythia-70m), +0.999984 (opt-125m), +0.999952 (distilgpt2) at alpha = 0.01, against +0.654540 / +0.887132 / +0.946743 / +0.645348 for the W_out-only direction that omits the Jacobian. So the JVP term is both necessary and correctly implemented. The rest of the kernel checks out on re-derivation: KL(base||steered) is quadratic in the perturbation and correctly demoted to _meta_ (it cannot distinguish +v from -v); the sign family uses a FIXED final-layer u so a layer can genuinely point the wrong way, while the ratio uses a per-layer u so both arms are measured along their own direction; the random control's denominator is the SAME functional as the numerator (signed mean over samples first, then median of |.| over draws).
comparable_reason: Over 8 models at the shipped config, steering_concept_over_random spans 0.0000 (SmolLM2-135M) to 2.3831 (distilgpt2) with sd 0.7067, against an RNG-only sd of 0.1347 on gpt2 -- so about 4% of the observed cross-model variance is pure RNG, which is tolerable, but the column is bottom-censored at 0 by the max(0, .) in the numerator and SmolLM2-135M sits exactly on that floor. directional_consistency SATURATES at exactly +1.0000 on 4 of the 8 models (distilgpt2, gpt2-medium, pythia-70m, opt-125m) and steering_sign_reversal at exactly 1.0000 on 5 of 8, so half the models are at a ceiling and cannot be ordered against each other. The architecture associations at n=8 are not significant (largest: concept_over_random rho -0.655 with n_layers, p ~ 0.08; semantic_effect rho -0.626 with vocab_size).
normalized_variant: steering_concept_over_random (concept effect / median magnitude of norm-matched random-direction effects) and steering_beats_random_frac
github_reason: Read both released codebases. RepE's control pipeline (repe/rep_control_*) injects a reading vector into the residual stream at chosen layers exactly as BLME's steering hook does, and activation_additions does the same for activation steering. Neither publishes the estimand BLME reports: RepE evaluates with a downstream classifier or generation judge, activation_additions with generated-text scoring. BLME never generates, and its logit-space projection with the LayerNorm Jacobian, the norm-matched random control and the data-defined semantic anchors are BLME's own. I could not run either head-to-head on this quantity, hence PARTIAL. What I did instead is verify the estimand against ground truth (the cosines above).
paper_reason: Zou et al. and Turner et al. report generation-based steering successes and downstream accuracies on instruct models; no published number corresponds to a signed logit-space projection ratio against a norm-matched random control. A legitimate NONE.
confounds_reason: Measured over 8 models (distilgpt2, gpt2, gpt2-medium, pythia-70m, pythia-160m, opt-125m, SmolLM2-135M, Qwen2.5-0.5B): steering_concept_over_random spearman +0.101 (d_model), -0.655 (n_layers), +0.221 (vocab_size); directional_consistency +0.068 / -0.494 / +0.177; steering_semantic_effect -0.038 / -0.037 / -0.626. None significant at n=8 (needs |rho| ~ 0.71 for p<0.05). The depth-leaning sign of the concept_over_random association is plausible mechanically -- test_layers is a FIXED five-point sample of depth, so deeper models are probed at sparser relative positions -- but I cannot establish it at this n. SUSPECTED, not CONFIRMED.
defects: THE PROBE-SUBSET SWING REPRODUCES EXACTLY, and the fix removes it on the bundled path. Rotating a caller-supplied 3-of-8 window over the SAME bundled triples on gpt2: steering_concept_over_random 2.8552154 [0:3] / 2.5901193 [2:5] / 0.3733647 [3:6] / 0.2218628 [4:7] / 1.8347576 [5:8], i.e. a 12.87x swing, with directional_consistency +1.0000 / +0.3983 / -0.1061 / -0.2000 / +0.6000 -- matching the reported 2.8552 -> 0.2219 and +1.0000 -> -0.2000 to every printed digit. With NO contrastive dataset (the study's actual situation) num_samples=3 and num_samples=8 now give BIT-IDENTICAL output (steering_concept_over_random 1.0527134431447898 in both) and _meta_n_probe_triples = 8. The swing can still recur for a CALLER-SUPPLIED dataset, which is still subsetted at num_samples; _meta_probe_set_is_bundled records which path ran.

THE _N_RAND_DRAWS_DEFAULT = 32 CLAIM IS WRONG ON BOTH COUNTS, and the red team is right. I measured it by shimming torch.randn inside the module so the per-layer seed stream shifts by a fixed offset (verified faithful: at offset 0 the patched run reproduces the unpatched run bit-for-bit, 1.0527134431447898). Over independent RNG streams on gpt2 at the CURRENT 8-triple config: 8 draws -> mean 1.0005, sd 0.4013, range 117.6% of the mean; 32 draws -> mean 0.8643, sd 0.1347, range 47.6% of the mean; 128 draws -> mean 0.8744, sd 0.1169, range 39.9% of the mean. So (a) 32 draws does NOT land at 2.56 -- that figure was measured on the pre-fix 3-triple probe set and is now stale by 3x; (b) it is NOT stable -- the coefficient of variation is 15.6%, and going to 128 draws cuts the sd only 1.15x where 1/sqrt(n) predicts 2x, so the dispersion has a FLOOR near sd 0.12 that more draws do not remove. The red team's 'range 53% of the mean, no convergence at 128' matches my 47.6% and my non-convergence; their absolute sd 0.4343 is consistent with mine in relative terms (their CV 17.0% vs my 15.6%).

THE FLOOR HAS A STRUCTURAL CAUSE the draw count cannot fix: the headline is a MEDIAN OVER THE FIVE TESTED LAYERS of a per-layer ratio (test_layers = [0, L/4, L/2, 3L/4, L-1]). As the denominators jitter, the median jumps between different layers' ratios, and a median over five points does not average down. At 128 draws the six stream realizations were 0.8011 / 0.8611 / 0.7205 / 1.0690 / 0.8889 / 0.9056 -- crossing 1.0, the value at which the task's own docstring says 'the steering is not concept-specific'. gpt2 therefore cannot be distinguished from 'no concept specificity' at any draw count.

THE EARLIER GREEN'S REASONING STAYS REFUTED, but only partly by the probe set. With the whole 8-triple set, directional_consistency is exactly +1.0000 on 4 of 8 models -- so the saturation is real and common -- but it is +0.0320 on gpt2 (directional_success_rate 0.40, i.e. 2 of 5 layers steer AGAINST the concept) and +0.2000 on SmolLM2-135M. 'Positive at every layer of every model' is false on the current code and the current probe set.

alpha = 1.0 is at the edge of the linear regime on at least one model: cos(delta_logits, u) falls from +0.989663 at alpha=0.01 to +0.943320 at alpha=1.0 on pythia-70m, while gpt2, opt-125m and distilgpt2 stay at +0.9999. The linearisation the whole estimand rests on is therefore model-dependent at the shipped alpha.

steering_concept_over_random is bottom-censored: the numerator is max(0, dir_pos[l]), so a model whose median tested layer steers the wrong way reads exactly 0.0000 (SmolLM2-135M does). Zero is not distinguishable from 'slightly wrong way' or 'very wrong way'.
CONFIG: the study still writes num_samples: 8 for a set the harness now uses whole regardless. Harmless, but it implies the knob controls something on the bundled path when it does not.
fix: Replace the _N_RAND_DRAWS_DEFAULT comment with numbers a rerun gives on the current probe set (32 draws -> 0.8643 +/- 0.1347 on gpt2, CV 15.6%, not 2.56 and not stable), and emit the across-draw dispersion as a _meta_ column so a caller can see that gpt2's 0.86 +/- 0.13 straddles the 1.0 decision point. Since the residual dispersion is the outer median over five layers rather than the draw count, either test more layers or report the per-layer ratios' distribution instead of their median -- raising n_random_draws past 32 buys only 1.15x. Record cos(delta_logits, u) at the shipped alpha as a linearity check (it is +0.943 on pythia-70m against +0.9999 elsewhere).
